name: Live Nation Entertainment
description: Live Nation promotes about 55,000 concerts and festivals a year (159 million fans in 2025), owns or operates and books venues, runs Ticketmaster (the ticket agency for arenas, stadiums, teams and other promoters), and sells sponsorships and advertising against all that fan traffic. It says it is the largest live-music promoter in the world. Revenue is dominated by the concert business (83 percent) but profit is not: promotion pays artists guarantees and costs that eat most of ticket revenue, while Ticketmaster (a fee on each ticket sold for clients, 37 percent margin) and sponsorship (58 percent operating margin) together produce about three quarters of segment profit from 17 percent of revenue. A major overhang is the US antitrust case: the Department of Justice and states sued in 2024 seeking divestiture of Ticketmaster; the company settled with the US on injunctive and structural terms in March 2026 and took a $450M charge in H1 2026 after a jury verdict against it for the remaining states on April 15, 2026.

businessLines.name: Concerts
businessLines.how: Fans pay for tickets (event revenue is deferred until the show) and buy concessions, parking, premium seats and merchandise at venues; Live Nation pays artists a guaranteed amount and/or a share of sales and covers production, so promotion is high-revenue and low-margin, while venue operations (concessions, parking, premium seating, rent) carry higher margins.
businessLines.description: Global promotion of live music events in owned, operated and rented venues, venue operations, music festivals, and management services for artists; about 55,000 events and 159 million fans in 2025.

revenue.note: Including intersegment revenue; FY2024 $19,024.3M (+10%); 83% of total revenue

businessLines.revenueNote: Including intersegment revenue; FY2024 $19,024.3M (+10%); 83% of total revenue

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $529.7M (2.8%). Segment operating income was only $85.5M in 2025 (a $381.9M loss in 2024 with the Astroworld charge). Share is of the three segments' AOI sum of $2,666.7M before corporate expenses.

businessLines.name: Ticketing (Ticketmaster)
businessLines.how: Venues and event owners sign multi-year (typically three to five years) exclusive ticketing contracts; for each ticket sold, buyers pay a service fee on top of the face value and Ticketmaster keeps its share while the client keeps the ticket price. Driven by the number of fee-bearing tickets and fee per ticket, with little direct cost per additional ticket.
businessLines.description: Primary ticketing agency for venues, promoters, teams and leagues in many countries; also ticket resale.

businessLines.name: Sponsorship & Advertising
businessLines.how: Brands pay annual or multi-year fees for access to fans (naming rights, signage, festival and venue sponsorship, digital placement); costs are mostly fulfillment, so margins are high.
businessLines.description: Sponsor programs across concerts, festivals, venues and ticketing platforms; venue naming rights; advertising on Live Nation and Ticketmaster websites.
